claim.quote: Measurement of Neutrino and Antineutrino Oscillations Using Beam and Atmospheric Data in MINOS

date.note: Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 110, 251801 (2013). `date` is the arXiv v1 submission date, earlier than the journal publication (A9: the display date is the earliest sourced public date).

key_value_text.quote: we measure \mbox{$|\Delta m^2}| = \unit[2.41^{+0.09}_{-0.10}) \times 10^{-3}]{eV^{2}}$} and $\sin^{2}/!/left(2\theta \right) = 0.950^{+0.035}_{-0.036}$ ... we measure antineutrino parameters of $|\Delta \bar{m}^2| = \unit[(2.50 ^{+0.23}_{-0.25}) \times 10^{-3}]{eV^{2}}$
key_value_text.value: |Δm²| = (2.41 +0.09/−0.10)×10⁻³ eV², sin²(2θ) = 0.950 +0.035/−0.036 from combined beam and atmospheric-neutrino data, assuming identical neutrino/antineutrino parameters; separately, |Δm̄²| = (2.50 +0.23/−0.25)×10⁻³ eV² for antineutrinos

name: Measurement of Neutrino and Antineutrino Oscillations Using Beam and Atmospheric Data in MINOS

significance.locator: arXiv:1304.6335, abstract (no single significance/sigma reported for a parameter measurement)
significance.note: A parameter measurement, not a discovery/observation with a single reported significance.

summary.plain: MINOS combined its own accelerator-beam data with atmospheric neutrinos to measure how muon neutrinos and antineutrinos disappear on the way to the detector, and found the neutrino and antineutrino mass splittings in excellent agreement. The paper calls these the world's most precise measurements to date of the mass splittings for both.
summary.technical: Combined NuMI beam and atmospheric-neutrino analysis: |Δm²|=(2.41+0.09-0.10)x10^-3 eV^2, sin^2(2θ)=0.950+0.035-0.036 (identical ν/ν̄ assumption); separate antineutrino fit gives |Δm̄²|=(2.50+0.23-0.25)x10^-3 eV^2, sin^2(2θ̄)=0.97+0.03-0.08, using 37.88 kton-years of atmospheric data plus beam exposure.

title: Measurement of Neutrino and Antineutrino Oscillations Using Beam and Atmospheric Data in MINOS
why_it_matters: The paper notes that MINOS can separate neutrinos and antineutrinos event by event and, coupled with the world's only set of long-baseline accelerator antineutrino data, allows a comparison of the neutrino and antineutrino mass splittings, which it finds in excellent agreement: |Δm²| − |Δm̄²| = (0.12 +0.24 −0.26)×10⁻³ eV².
